notes: Auto-Restore is gone from the picker. A customer is Monitor or Off. Drift still raises a case, and the case now opens a Guided restore: the exact policy changes to make, in order, with the values, ready to follow in the Entra admin centre. The same guide sits on the backup drawer and inside the investigation, so it is reachable from wherever you noticed the drift.

Install the backend update first, or with this one. This portal reads the deployment's Conditional Access write setting from the backend, and a backend too old to send it is read as read-only — so the screens would tell you Basewiser does not write while an older backend still would.
The backup screens say backup. The Snapshots column is now Backups, and the customer report's tile with it; the word meant the same thing and the product had two names for one idea.

Drift still raises a case, and the case now opens a Guided restore: the exact policy changes to make, in order, with the values, ready to follow in the Entra admin centre. The same guide sits on the backup drawer and inside the investigation, so it is reachable from wherever you noticed the drift.

Install the backend update first, or with this one. This portal reads the deployment's Conditional Access write setting from the backend, and a backend too old to send it is read as read-only — so the screens would tell you Basewiser does not write while an older backend still would.
The backup screens say backup. The Snapshots column is now Backups, and the customer report's tile with it; the word meant the same thing and the product had two names for one idea.

You can run an Azure sweep when you want one. Sweep Azure now sits on every Azure page for a customer — the theme pages and Subscriptions — and reads that one customer's subscriptions straight away instead of waiting for the nightly run. A customer you have just connected, or just fixed something for, can be made to show a posture number in a single click, from the page where its absence is visible. It tells you what it is doing while it runs and what came back, including a sweep that only partly succeeded.

Install the backend update first, or at the same time as this one. An older backend ignores the per-customer scope this button sends: the sweep would read every customer you have rather than the one whose page you are on, and would not be able to explain a sweep that found nothing to do.

Download PDF works in an installed portal. The assessment artifact — the document you hand a customer, with what we found, what it would take to fix and what it costs — prints on the server, so every operator on every device gets identical bytes rather than whatever their own browser would have produced. The browser that prints it now ships inside the portal image, which is about 300 MB larger and needs the resources the install docs state.

Posture is told per category and over time. Entra and Azure carry their own score, their own 30-day trend and their own count of what actually closed this period — never one blended number — and every finding names the check that produced it and what that check measures. The customer-facing documents carry the same story.

Where our check catalogue changed inside a trend window, both customer documents now mark that day on the chart and count movement from the mark onwards, so a re-grading on our side never reads as the customer's own improvement. Install the backend update first or with this one: until you do, the per-category trend, the closed count, the check citations and the catalogue stamp have nothing to draw on and are left out of the pages entirely.

An opportunity whose evidence can no longer be read now stays in your pipeline instead of moving to Delivered & resolved. Losing sight of a deal is not the customer fixing it, and work you are actively selling should not file itself away because a sweep failed. It carries no value while the evidence is out of reach — counted as open, left out of the pipeline total — unless you have quoted it by hand, in which case your own price is kept.

A won project whose evidence went dark stays in Delivered & resolved, but is badged Unconfirmed rather than Delivered and now shows its price. Won this quarter was already counting that deal while the row itself showed no money, so the tile and the list disagreed about the same project. Both kinds of unconfirmed row now link straight to that customer's connection, which is where the cause is, and neither can be turned into a proposal — the document would carry no findings and no price.

Install this before or with the backend update. In the other order an older portal reads a won project whose evidence went dark as a plain Delivered with its evidence cleared, which is the claim this release exists to stop.

Proposals no longer print a garbled scope line. Every item of included scope now carries its own written sentence, or is deliberately left out because the project's standing scope already promises it. Previously the line was assembled at print time by cutting a phrase off the observation and appending to it, which composed a readable sentence only for the two Conditional Access lines it was built around — the Azure waste proposal reached a customer as three clauses run together.

The connection overlay's verdict now reads each half of a connection on its own. It previously answered "is there work left" and reported the answer as "not connected yet", so a customer who was connected but incomplete, or connected and since removed, read the same as one who had never started. Four states were wrong; three of nine sample customers rendered incorrectly.

Install the backend update alongside this one. Without it the portal still works, but falls back to printing the raw observation for an included-scope line rather than the written sentence — which is the garbled line the first note describes.

A customer you have invited to Microsoft 365 but who has not approved yet now has a row of their own. Until now they had none — the approval link is the same for every customer, so nothing about handing it over recorded who it went to, and a customer only exists once they approve, leaving days in which the portal showed nothing at all. Type their address when you hand the link over and they appear under Invited on the Customers list, with how long they have been waiting and who sent it. The row clears itself when they approve, and Dismiss is there for one that landed somewhere it could not see. The address stays optional — leave it blank and you get the same link and the same three actions, with nothing recorded. Install the backend update first: without it the address is accepted and quietly not kept.

The side menu now shows how much each findings section holds. Entra ID, Azure and Conditional Access each carry a number beside them, the way the Inbox already did and the way a customer's own menu already does, so you can see where the work is without opening each section to find out. The numbers are the same totals the section pages themselves show, so a number in the menu cannot disagree with the page it takes you to. A section sitting at zero shows no number at all, because a zero reads as a measurement and a section can be empty either because it is clean or because nothing is connected to it yet — the page tells you which. The Inbox keeps its red number and is still the only one shown when the menu is collapsed to the narrow rail, because several red numerals down a narrow column read as several alarms rather than one.

What's new is now a history rather than a single list. Every release you have not installed yet gets its own section, newest first, with its date, how many changes it carries and the changes written out in full — so if you have skipped a few, you can read what each one was instead of only the newest. Above them it names the build you are running and the build you would be on, portal and backend side by side, so you can see exactly what the update moves. Starting the update from in there now closes it and leaves the job with the card in the corner, which was already showing you the same progress.

The update card's progress no longer runs ahead of itself. The percentage used to leap to 95 and then sit there for the best part of a minute while the new build came up, which reads as though it has stalled when it has not; the number and the bar now move together and both follow the stage the update is actually in. While an update is waiting for you the card shows a marker travelling along its top edge, and the step in progress is marked as it happens.

Opening Opportunities from inside a customer no longer looks like the page reloading. The menu on the left stayed on that customer, but on the way there it visibly flicked out to the main menu and back, which made a normal click look like something had gone wrong. It stays put now, and opening one of that customer's deals keeps it too. The main menu still returns when you open Opportunities across the whole portfolio, or widen the customer filter past the one you came in with.

Azure now has a page of its own across your whole portfolio, beside Entra ID. It shows your worst Azure exposure across every connected customer, worst first, and a row clicks through to the customer and the theme it came from. Subscriptions are counted rather than listed: the page is already grouped by customer, and stacking subscriptions underneath would be a second level of grouping in one flat table. There is no Critical card, because Azure has no Critical severity and a card that could only ever read zero tells you nothing. A portfolio with no Azure connected is told so in a sentence, never shown a zero that reads as clean. Install the backend release of the same date first, or the page opens empty.

The side menu now says Entra ID where it said Identity — in your portfolio menu, in each customer's menu, and on the Entra ID health heading. What sits under that name is Tenant settings, Applications, Group hygiene and Auth weakness, which Identity only ever described about half of. Nothing about the addresses has changed, so your existing links and bookmarks still work, and Identity Health stays the name of the product you are billed for.

The update banner has moved to the bottom-right corner and now tells you what it is doing. It used to be a strip across the top that pushed the page down when it appeared and back up when it went, moving whatever you were reading at the time. It now sits over the page instead, so nothing shifts. While an update runs it names each step as it happens — the portal, the backend, then waiting for the new build to serve — and it waits for the new version to actually answer before reloading, rather than reloading on a timer. An update that fails now keeps the card, says what went wrong in the words the server used, and offers Try again, instead of disappearing and leaving you to guess.

Onboarding a customer is now a page rather than a window. It opens with one line saying what onboarding is, the steps laid out so you can see where you are, and what approving grants written out beside the work instead of folded behind a link. The old window was cramped, and a stray click outside it lost whatever you were part-way through; this one has its own address, so you can leave it, go and do something in Azure, and come back to where you were.

Onboarding now asks how much Azure to ask for, because the two answers are not the same thing. Per subscription covers only the subscriptions the person who approves is an Owner on — anything they are not an Owner on is silently left out. All subscriptions, and future ones covers every subscription in the tenant including ones created later, and needs a Global Administrator who has raised their own Azure access first: the page names the toggle they turn on, where to find it, and tells them they can turn it back off once you are connected. Microsoft 365 is step one and is a complete onboarding on its own. Azure is step two, and Skip is a normal answer — you can send that link from the customer's page whenever they are ready.

Adding a customer by typing in their tenant ID is gone. It never opened a consent screen: it created an empty row that collected nothing until the customer approved anyway, which is the same approval the link asks for. If you used it to keep track of customers you had invited but who had not consented yet, that is a real gap and it is being fixed properly rather than left to a hand-typed row.

The first-run setup screen and the onboarding page now match: the same step list down the left, and the buttons on a bar at the foot of the screen. On setup those buttons could previously shift down the page when a step grew, so they were never quite where you last left them.

Every customer now has an Opportunities entry in their side menu. It opens your pipeline filtered to that customer: the same page, the same rate card and the same proposal flow, narrowed to them — so the figure you quote a customer cannot disagree with the one in your portfolio.

The filters on Opportunities now narrow the four totals at the top, not just the tables beneath them. Filtered to one customer, the open pipeline, proposed value and won-this-quarter figures are that customer's. A customer with nothing worth selling yet is told by name rather than shown an empty table. Install the backend release of the same date first, or won totals will read low.

A section heading in a customer's side menu now closes the section you are inside. Clicking Identity, Azure or Conditional Access while already in it returns you to that customer's overview and collapses it; until now it did nothing at all.

Every customer page now says which customer it is. The name sits at the top as a proper heading, with the domain, tenant ID and the last Conditional Access backup listed under it. Until now the only thing naming the customer was the highlighted item in the side menu, so two customers' pages looked identical at a glance.

The connection window is now a screen you can come back to. It opens with one sentence answering the whole thing, separates what is settled from what is still outstanding rather than walking you through steps you have already done, and a finished half collapses to a single dated line instead of a green tick. It is also reachable from the customer list and the side menu, not just the customer overview. The command you hand a customer to confirm their Azure access no longer reports an error when it has in fact worked.

Azure findings are on the customer overview, and the two Azure projects read as projects. The overview's fourth tile is now Azure findings — a dash rather than a zero until a sweep has run — and both it and Identity findings click through to what the number is made of. Azure exposure and Azure cost now carry their own pitch and proposal text rather than appearing with the section blank.

Azure is in the portal. Every customer who has connected Azure now has Azure pages beside their Microsoft 365 ones — findings grouped into the six themes and broken down per subscription, an inventory of every subscription Basewiser can read, and a Mute for the ones you do not want counted or shown to the customer. The nightly sweep has been collecting since 9 August, so these pages open with history behind them rather than empty. You can also set how often the sweep runs across your whole portfolio — daily, every two days, or weekly — and the two Azure opportunities, exposure and cost, now appear beside the Microsoft 365 ones.

A half-connected customer now says so. When Azure was approved on some of a customer's subscriptions and not others, the connection window showed a green tick and the words "Nothing to do" — directly above the sentence saying a subscription was not being monitored. It now counts that customer as half-connected, names the subscriptions nobody granted, and shows the exact command their Azure Owner runs to finish the job. No new invite is needed, and running it twice changes nothing.

You can ask Azure directly whether access landed. A new "Re-check access in Azure" asks Azure itself what Basewiser can read, rather than repeating what was last stored — so when a customer runs the command and says "done", you can confirm it in seconds instead of waiting for the next nightly sweep. The button beside it is now called Refresh, because re-reading is what it always did.

Your portal now stays on the version you installed. Until now a deployment could quietly swap itself to a newer build whenever Azure restarted it — mid-session, unannounced, and with nothing in Azure recording that it had happened. From this release it stays where it is until you choose to update.

You can also now see which build a deployment is on by looking at it in Azure. Previously the only way to answer that was to sign in to the portal and read the version in the sidebar, which meant support could not check it for you.

No action needed. The first time an administrator opens the portal after this update, it records the version it is already running and stops following the moving reference. The code that is serving does not change — only the label Azure keeps. New installations get this from the start.

Fixes a fault that would have stopped your first customer connecting their Azure. If your deployment was installed before Azure onboarding shipped, the page Microsoft returns the customer to was still behind the portal sign-in — so the customer met a login screen they have no account for, and the invite was used up. Nothing showed this until it happened.

No action needed. The portal now checks and repairs its own sign-in exclusions when an administrator opens it, and again whenever you install an update. It only ever adds the two onboarding pages, and only those two.

A customer whose Azure is connected no longer reads "Pending" on their Overview. It now reads "Connected", with a line saying that Basewiser does not scan Azure yet — so there is nothing there to wait for. Microsoft 365 still reads "Pending" until its first scan finishes, because that one does finish.
Install this together with the backend release of the same date.

Settings has a new Basewiser app tab. From it you can re-activate the app, which is how it picks up permissions Basewiser has added since you first set it up — previously there was no way to do this once the app existed. It tells you what will change before you confirm.
If re-activating ever creates a second app registration instead of updating yours, the portal now says so plainly and tells you to stop, rather than reporting it as a success.
Install this together with the backend release of the same date. The portal's Azure pages call backend routes that a backend from before this release does not have.

Connect a customer's Azure. Onboarding now carries both invites on one screen: Microsoft 365 as before, and a new Azure one that a subscription Owner opens to grant Basewiser read-only access. Reopen it as often as you like — it shows how far each customer has got, and connecting Azure does not change their Azure bill.
A customer nobody can look at now says so. Access that has lapsed gets its own health band on both the Microsoft 365 and Azure halves, instead of quietly looking healthy.

Install this together with the backend release of the same date. This pair changes how the Deployment signs in to its own storage, and a portal from before it cannot read the setting that replaces the old one — the Get help page's backend update would report the storage account as missing.

Nothing changes in what you see or do. The work is underneath: your Deployment now proves who it is to its own database and message queue using the identity Azure gives it, instead of holding copies of the account keys in its settings. Those keys have been removed.

Update the portal and the backend together for this one. The address the portal uses to ask the backend for data has changed, so a portal on this version talking to a backend on the previous one cannot load anything — every page will say it failed. Both updates are offered under Get help; run them one after the other and the portal comes back. Reinstalling from the setup script does both at once.

Everywhere the portal said “fleet”, it now says “portfolio”. The Dashboard is headed Portfolio overview, the Licenses table totals read Portfolio total, and the backup schedule your customers inherit is the Portfolio default. A fleet is a set of vehicles; what the word actually named here is the set of customers you carry, and it read oddly next to “Customer health” on the same screen.

Where a sentence can name the thing itself, it now does that instead: the Dashboard cards read “Across all customers” rather than reaching for a word for the group. A deployment set up to call them environments rather than customers gets that word — the wording follows the label you chose.

Your dashboard sparklines start empty after this update, and the backup default schedule and the Opportunities rate card go back to their defaults. They are kept under names that changed with this release, so the old ones are no longer read. The sparklines refill on their own over the next day or so; the schedule and the rate card need setting once more.

The Customers list is now split by who you are paying for. Customers on a seat sit in the main table; the ones you have consented but are not billing yet sit in their own dashed section below it, headed “Connected, not billed”, with the same look the Billing page already uses for them. That section replaces the per-row Status column, which repeated “Active” down every row of a healthy fleet to say something the split now says once.

A customer you are not billing shows an em-dash for Health and Alerts rather than an invented verdict, because nothing is scanned until you activate it — and its row now takes you to the activation flow instead of a page the seat gate would refuse. If you opened a checkout and never finished it, that row is marked “Checkout open”, since nothing else in the portal tells you that work is still hanging.

Status on Backup & Restore and on Customers is drawn the way severity has been since the last release: a small colour swatch and the word, not a filled chip. A column where every row carries a chip is a wall of colour in which nothing stands out; the swatch keeps the signal and lets the things that need attention be the things you see. Size bands keep their chip — they are labels, not verdicts.
Backup & Restore and Customers both gain the customer filter pill that Licenses and Opportunities already had, so every fleet page narrows to a named customer the same way.
On Licenses, the reclaimable-spend card now trends its own series instead of borrowing the total-cost line, so the sparkline matches the number above it.
Prices are stated as NOK-anchored and charged in your local currency, and the currency shown across the portal follows that.

The currency and timezone pickers are redesigned, and the two places they appear — the top bar and the first-run setup — now use the same one. Region headings stay put while you scroll the timezone list, each row carries its UTC offset as a small badge, and the raw zone name ("Europe/Oslo") no longer sits under every city: it is stated once at the foot of the list instead.

In first-run setup, "How you read the portal" now shows currency and timezone as two aligned rows. The timezone dropdown used to run wider than the currency buttons above it, and the note about rates being indicative was hidden behind a hover — both are fixed.

Every list now leads with its verdict, and the column header stays put as you scroll. Identity and Conditional Access lead with severity, Licenses with how much of its spend is wasted (Heavy, Some, Minor, Clean), Opportunities with how strong the case is (Strong, Good, Thin). The Inbox no longer splits cases into severity headings: severity is a sortable column instead, so a critical case can never sit inside a collapsed section.

Fixed a Licenses data-trust hole. A customer whose license data failed to load used to render as an ordinary row with nothing to reclaim, and its missing spend was quietly added into the fleet total. The page now says when a customer's data is incomplete, and the totals say so too.

Tidier list pages. In the By customer views the per-customer severity tally now sits next to the customer name instead of floating out over the other columns, the explanatory paragraph above the Licenses and Opportunities tables is gone, and the By severity / By customer switch no longer stretches across the page.

Severity now looks the same everywhere. Identity, Conditional Access, the per-customer finding tabs, the Dashboard and the monthly customer report all show a small colour square and the word, matching the Inbox, instead of a filled coloured tag. In a list where every row has a severity, the filled tags drowned each other out.

The portal now calls a piece of work you triage a case everywhere, instead of switching between case and incident depending on the screen. The Dashboard's open-work table and the search box wording follow the Inbox.

The Inbox list is rebuilt. Cases are now grouped under Critical, High, Medium and Low headings, each row carries at most one status word instead of up to four coloured tags, and Category is a sortable column. The column header stays put as you scroll.

By customer now ranks customers by how much work they hold, not just by their single worst case, so a customer with a pile of medium cases no longer sits below one with a single high. A summary at the top shows where the work is and jumps you to any customer.

Case titles now start with what changed rather than an account name, so a title reads "Global Administrator granted to ola@example.com" instead of leading with the address. Only new cases use the new wording.
Housekeeping only. The sample customers and email addresses used in the built-in demo data are now made-up names. Nothing about how the portal works has changed.

Setting up the portal is now one flow instead of two separate windows that competed over which showed first. It greets you, asks only for the things still missing, and hands you to the tour at the end.
The tour now starts when you finish setup. It used to open behind the setup window, so it looked like nothing happened.
You pick your currency and timezone during setup, so prices and times read the way you expect from the first screen.

Setting up the portal is now one flow instead of two separate windows that competed over which showed first. It greets you, asks only for the things still missing, and hands you to the tour at the end.
The tour now starts when you finish setup. It used to open behind the setup window, so it looked like nothing happened.
You pick your currency and timezone during setup, so prices and times read the way you expect from the first screen.
A customer's Health pill now shows how serious their open cases are. A customer with one critical case no longer looks the same as one with only minor ones.

A policy's History tab now shows its real change log. It used to ask for a record the backend never served, so the tab stayed empty. A renamed policy keeps its history, and a deleted policy shows the deletion instead of quietly dropping out.
Closed cases no longer push open ones off the Inbox list, and the Closed tab now says when it is only showing the most recent cases.

The portal now has a proper error page with a retry, and a proper Not found page. A customer that is missing is reported as missing and a backend that is down is reported as down, instead of the two looking the same.

Adding a customer now asks for consent once, for the single Basewiser app. The tenant page used to run three separate checks, and a check that failed could show a consent warning on a customer that was actually fine.
The 24 hour graphs now draw one point per hour instead of eight, so the line matches the range you picked.
The activity feed filter is now called Area instead of Bundle.

The prompt shown when no customer is streaming data yet is reworked. It drops the word 'seat' and lays out the real two steps, add a customer then activate it, lighting the step you're on. With no customers yet it points you to add your first one; once one is onboarded it points you straight to activating it.
That banner can now be dismissed just for the current session and comes back next time you open the portal, so the only next step is never hidden for good.

During the guided tour, when you have no customers yet, a sample customer row now appears again so the 'Size and price' step has something to point at. It could go missing when the tour opened the Customers page for you.

The first-run experience now runs in the right order. You finish naming your identity and setting up the Basewiser app first, and only then does the welcome and guided tour appear. Before, the tour could be missed behind the setup screen.

The setup screen is clearer. It now says your display name can be changed later in Settings, and explains that the Basewiser app is the single app each customer you onboard consents to, which is what lets Basewiser read their tenant data.

Guided tour polish. The step footer uses a progress bar instead of a row of dots that overflowed the card, the Back and Next buttons now match, and the highlight around each step sits a little tighter.
Fixed a false "A backend update is available" banner that kept showing for a backend version you already run. The portal now reads the installed backend version reliably.
Installing an update now waits until the new version is actually serving before it finishes, instead of reloading on a timer.

The onboarding tour now follows a logical first-run flow and highlights the currency and timezone controls in the header bar. When the account has no tenants yet, a demo row appears during the tour so every step has something to point at.
Report pages now use the same full width as the rest of the portal. The pipeline report is renamed to Opportunities.
Feature descriptions across the portal and marketing site now reflect the full scanning scope — including application security, auth weaknesses, and tenant hardening.
Redesigned tenant sidebar with section navigation, inline customer switcher with health indicators, and wider page layouts for larger monitors.

Demo mode now previews the full Identity detection set, including the new Tenant settings findings and the guest / AD-synced privileged-account cards, so evaluations show everything the scanners can find.

New Tenant settings category in Identity: flags user consent open to all apps, guest invites open to everyone, self-service app registration, and tenants running with no Conditional Access and no security defaults.
Privileged access now also flags guest accounts holding privileged roles and AD-synced accounts holding privileged roles (cloud-only admin guidance).

The fleet Identity Health list now shows each finding's count in parentheses after its name (for example "Stale guest accounts (12)"), matching the Conditional Access list so the two read the same way.

The fleet tables now share one consistent design: Identity Health, Conditional Access, Backup & Restore, Opportunities and the Billing Subscription and Invoices tables use the same column layout, sorting and spacing, so every list reads and behaves the same way.

Fixed the Invoices table alignment — the amount now shows its currency right beside the value, and the Amount, Status and Receipt columns sit neatly together instead of drifting apart on wide screens.

New: a monthly customer report for every tenant, opened from the tenant menu as Monthly report. One page a customer can read: the security posture score with a 30-day trend, what was caught and handled this period with response times, open cases and findings, what is monitored, and backup status.

The report is a designed document in the Basewiser brand, and Print / Save as PDF turns it into a dark A4 PDF. Every figure is read from the same live data the dashboard shows, so the report can never disagree with the portal.

New Identity finding under Risky users: 'Users flagged at risk'. It surfaces the accounts Microsoft Entra ID Protection flags as at risk, with each account's recent risky sign-ins and a one-click link into Entra to investigate. Needs Entra ID P2; on tenants without it the card stays hidden.

The Identity tab's recent-admins list now covers every privileged role Microsoft flags, not just Global Admin and Tier-0, with a new Tier column showing each role's blast radius. It's renamed 'Privileged roles added in the last 30 days'.
Turning Guard off, or down from Auto-Restore to Monitor, now opens an inbox case so the change is acknowledged — not just a quiet line in the activity feed.

New inbox case when someone is added to a group that grants a privileged role (for example a group that holds Global Admin). They inherit the role with no direct role-assignment record, so the normal grant alert can't see it — this closes that gap.

New on the Identity tab under Privileged access: 'Administrators added in the last 30 days'. A rolling review list of accounts granted Global Administrator or a Tier-0 role recently, showing permanent versus eligible and whether the grant came directly or through a group. Entries drop off on their own once a grant is older than the window.

The Inbox now flags exclusion-group changes: when an account (or a whole group) is added to a group that an enabled Conditional Access policy excludes, a case opens naming who was added, by whom, which policies no longer cover the account, and whether it signed in while outside them. The case page never suggests a backup restore for these, because a restore cannot undo a membership change; removing the member from the group closes the gap, and doing so resolves the case automatically.
Sparkline curves on the dashboard and licenses cards no longer overshoot: a flat series stays flat and a spike settles without dipping past its baseline.

On the Identity category charts, hovering a segment whose label wraps to two lines no longer nudges the legend and the rest of the card down. The number-and-label readout beside the honeycomb now keeps the same height whether it shows the one-line total or a two-line hovered label.

The Identity category charts (Multi-factor authentication, Stale identities, Privileged access, Group hygiene) now use a fixed-size honeycomb ribbon instead of one hexagon per person. Every chart is the same compact height, so a pair of charts lines up and their totals sit on one line, and a large tenant no longer draws a wall of hexagons. The exact numbers stay in the total beside the chart and in the legend.

The chart legend now sits in two tidy columns packed to the left, so short labels no longer leave a large empty gap across the card, and a long factor name still fits without running the card's full width.
The fleet Licenses "Total monthly cost" card no longer prints the start and end dates under its sparkline.

Fixed the Alert volume chart. It was drawing a smoothed curve that spread a single alert across the whole week, so a day with no alerts could still show a peak. It now draws one bar per day matching the actual number of alerts.

Fixed the licence cost graph on the Licenses page. A day with no snapshot was recorded as zero, which dropped the line to the floor and showed a false 100% decrease. A day without a snapshot now carries the last known cost instead.
The cost sparkline now prints the dates it covers at each end, so it is clear which period the graph is from.

Activate tenants: the user count and the size chip now line up in their own columns. They were right-aligned together as one group, so a shorter count or a shorter chip pushed the whole pair sideways and no two rows lined up. The already-active list uses the same columns, so both lists read as one table.
The Annual option now reads "2 months free" instead of the abbreviated, all-caps "2 MO FREE".
Fleet reports now download as a formatted Excel file with a proper header row and aligned columns. You can also pick a plain CSV for European or US Excel, and amounts follow your selected currency.
Fixed the Identity and Conditional Access reports, which were showing empty counts for every customer. They now show each customer's real findings.
On a customer's Licenses tab, seat utilisation now measures assigned seats against paid seats, so the percentage lines up with the seat counts next to it.

The Identity area has a new Applications section. It reviews the app registrations and enterprise apps in each customer's Microsoft Entra tenant and surfaces security risks, with the same drill-down and step-by-step fixes as the other findings.

Applications covers eight checks: credentials about to expire, apps holding tenant-wide permissions, insecure sign-in redirect URLs, risky consent grants, a new secret added to a privileged app, legacy sign-in flows, apps from unverified publishers, and stale or unused apps.
Stale apps are judged conservatively so an app that is quietly still in use is never flagged. An app is only listed when both its sign-in history and its credentials say it is no longer live.

Display fix: where a finding lists several values in one cell, such as the permissions an app holds or the roles a group grants, they now stack on separate lines instead of a "+N" badge, and the Guest and Member labels read as plain text.
The "You're connected" confirmation page a customer sees after granting consent now shows the Basewiser logo correctly, and no longer displays a "New tenant" placeholder as the organisation name.
The Customers page has a Refresh button next to Add tenant. Use it to pull in a customer that just finished onboarding, or whose name and size just resolved, without reloading the whole page.

On an incident, the policy membership explorer now shows the change only on the After side: Before is the plain baseline, and After marks what changed, with added accounts in green and removed accounts in red. A removed account reads as a normal row in Before and a red row in After.
Small layout fix on an incident's Live policy state: the Show technical changes and Open in tenant actions now sit at the bottom of the header, aligned with the description.

The incident page now shows the policy as a side-by-side Before change and After the change comparison, so you can read what each setting was and what it became at a glance. When Guard reverted an unauthorized change, the column that is live now is outlined in green.

Include and Exclude lists open in a searchable members explorer: switch between the before and after rosters, see the accounts that were added (green) or removed (red) floated to the top, and search or filter without the list resizing as you toggle.
The sign-ins-during-the-window card now shows each sign-in method and the location it came from, and every status tag across the page shares one size and shape, differing only in colour.

The Inbox incident page was redesigned for faster scanning. Case facts sit on one line under the title, three cards answer who made the change, where, and how long the exposure window was, and the policy view tells each setting's story in full sentences: baseline, while the change was live, now.

New incident timeline: events grouped by date with aligned clock times, quiet stretches shown as labelled breaks, and the sign-in check's completion as its own event. Sign-ins during the exposure window get their own card under the timeline, and an account whose name could not be resolved shows as Unresolved account with a copy button for its id, never a raw id.
The person behind a change shows with their display name, and while the audit lookup is still running the page says Identifying instead of claiming the actor is unknown.
On the Identity page's Privileged access tab, Permanent assignments now carry a red tag matching the green Eligible one, and rows line up at the same height.

New Group hygiene tab on each customer's Identity page. It surfaces the groups that can be granted Microsoft Entra directory roles (role-assignable groups): the roles each one grants (or none yet), its members and owners, and whether it is Tier-0. Empty groups that still grant a privileged role, and role-assignable groups with no owner, are flagged as the ones to review first.
Renamed the Identity 'Active risk' category to 'Risky users'.

New Authentication methods view on each customer's Identity tab: see who has registered which methods — Microsoft Authenticator, FIDO2 / passkeys, Windows Hello, certificates, hardware and software OATH tokens, Temporary Access Pass, SMS and phone — plus third-party and external providers shown by name. Each user carries a strength rating, a phishing-resistant marker, admin and SSPR (self-service password reset) flags, and last sign-in. Sort any column, filter by method (including 'No methods') or strength, and search by name; large tenants open on a weakest-first triage view with Show all.

Export CSV covers every user in the tenant — not just the on-screen sample — for compliance and audits. It's sourced from Microsoft's registration report, so it stays complete even for very large tenants.
Removed the unfinished Zero Trust tab from the customer view.

The report tables now speak the same design language as the rest of the portal: a customer's status shows as the standard status tag (like the Customers list), zero-counts render as a clean dash instead of rows of grey zeros, and only real signals carry colour — critical in red, high and drift in amber.

Reports is now a full surface: three new reports join Licensing — Posture (each customer's health status, Zero Trust score, findings by severity, alerts and backup freshness, worst-first), Identity (findings by severity and category — MFA gaps, stale identities, privileged access — with how many accounts they touch), and Conditional Access (findings split into drift versus policy hygiene). Every report works the same way: pick one customer, several or the whole fleet, download an Excel-ready CSV.

The Reports overview page is now a proper hub — one card per report showing the question it answers and what's inside — and the unfinished 'Custom reports' and 'Query performance' placeholders are gone.
The guided tour's Reports step now describes exactly what reports do.

Conditional Access: a policy's Include and Exclude assignment cards now share one clean, aligned design. Every target — users, groups, roles and 'All users' — gets a proper icon (the old 'All users' asterisk is gone), and the two columns line up at matching heights.
Opportunities: the 'Outcome' line on a project, and the Won and Status tiles, now use the same squared check mark as the rest of the portal — one consistent success mark everywhere.

Clearer wording when you stop billing a customer. You can cancel one tenant on its own without touching the others, and the portal now says exactly what happens: streaming stops right away, while billing stops at the end of the current period with no further charges. The same wording is corrected in the cancel confirmation, the Help center FAQ and the offboarding walkthrough.

The first-run guided tour now walks through the whole portal, not just onboarding. After adding a customer and activating a seat, it points out each place you'll work — the fleet Dashboard, Identity, Conditional Access, Licenses, Backup & Restore, the Inbox, Opportunities and Reports — one short step each, so a new operator sees everything the platform does from day one. Re-open it any time from Get help → 'Take the tour'.

Each opportunity now opens on a full-width page that puts the whole sales story on one screen: the pitch to read to the customer — the same words as the proposal — beside a private 'why it sells' note, the evidence with the hours each finding adds to the estimate, the full project scope and its outcome, and a plain price build-up (starting hours plus what the evidence adds).
A new 'More at this customer' panel shows the other open opportunities on the same tenant and their combined value, so you can propose them together and save the customer a second round.

Severity now uses the same tags as the rest of the portal (Critical, High, Medium, Low), and a layout pass tidied the page — the action buttons line up with the title, the small section notes sit under their headings, and the middot separators are gone.

The Opportunities page is redesigned to match the rest of the portal — a sortable table, the same status tags and colour key, and a clearer rate card: choose an hourly rate or a fixed price per project type, set starting and maximum hours in plain terms, and see the rate in your chosen display currency as you type.

Every opportunity now opens on its own page with room to read it: the full evidence from the customer's own tenant — each line linking straight to where it was found (Identity, Conditional Access or Licenses) — what the project covers, an internal note, and editable hours and price.
The client proposal now carries the portal's dark, branded look, ready to print or save as PDF and hand to the customer. Every figure across Opportunities follows the currency picker in the top bar.

New Opportunities page: the portal now turns what its scans find into ready-to-sell projects — each with the evidence behind it, a suggested effort, and a price from your own rate card (an hourly rate, or a fixed price per project type — editable right on the page).

One click generates a client-ready proposal for any opportunity: live evidence from the customer's own tenant, plain-language scope, and the investment — with payback math when the project saves the customer money. Print it or save as PDF.
Track each lead from new → proposed → won (or dismiss it). When a won project's evidence clears, it moves to Delivered — the value story you can show the customer at the next review.
Nothing is padded: opportunities only appear when there is enough real evidence to justify a project, and the page says so when your tenants are in good shape.

The fleet Identity Health, Conditional Access and Licenses cards now show the same up/down trend tag as the dashboard, so you can tell at a glance whether a number is rising or falling. Hover it to see the window it compares against — 7 days on Identity and Conditional Access, 30 days for license cost.
Inbox: the table header now sits on the same background as the rows, matching the other lists (it had a faint lighter band before).

The fleet Identity Health, Conditional Access and Licenses cards now show the same up/down trend tag as the dashboard, so you can tell at a glance whether a number is rising or falling. Hover it to see the window it compares against — 7 days on Identity and Conditional Access, 30 days for license cost.
Inbox: the table header now sits on the same background as the rows, matching the other lists (it had a faint lighter band before).
When no tenant has an active seat yet, a banner now points you to buy one — the portal stays free until you do.

Dashboard: the 'Open cases' card (which just repeated Active alerts) is now 'Active seats' — how many tenants are actively streaming data. A tenant's Identity tab swaps the 'Categories' tile for 'Affected accounts'.
The summary-card trend tags now show '0%' when a metric is steady instead of hiding, and hovering one tells you the window it compares against (e.g. 'vs 24 hours ago').

When you open a finding, its fix guide is much clearer to follow: the failed check now stands out in red, the steps read as one numbered procedure, and the 'How to fix' part sits in its own box, separated from the finding above it.
This applies everywhere a finding has a fix guide — Conditional Access, Identity and break-glass.

The Conditional Access page now matches the rest of the portal — consistent status tags and colours throughout, and the policy list is a proper sortable table (sort by policy, who it applies to, when it changed, or on/report/off). The cramped text on the right of each row has been cleaned up.
Tooltips on the Conditional Access page now use the portal's own styled tooltip instead of the plain grey system one.

Blue buttons and selected states left over from the old look are now neutral across the portal — for example Run backup, Activate, the active-tab underline, and the Licenses 'reclaimable' card's glow.

The Feedback panel is reworked — cleaner and on-theme, with a reply-to email and a clear list of what's attached. You can now paste a screenshot straight in (e.g. from Greenshot) or add an image file.
The Help drawer gained the missing FAQ link, and now switches topics correctly even when you're already on the Help page.
The dashboard's Open cases table now sorts on every column, like the other lists.

Customers: the Size column now leads the table, and a customer's user count stays readable even for very large tenants without crowding the next column. The old bundles filter — which no longer matched anything — is now a Status filter (Active, Pending or Not active).
Backup: the fleet schedule dialog is cleaner and uses plain wording, and you can now set the exact time backups run, shown in the timezone you picked in the top bar.

Getting started in the Help center is now a set of click-by-click walkthroughs — onboarding a customer, activating a seat, offboarding, break-glass accounts, backup & restore, triaging an Inbox alert, and restoring a Conditional Access change — each showing the exact controls to use.
Every dashboard and fleet summary card now carries a clear icon, and the tenant counts use a building icon instead of a people one.
Summary cards now build in when you open a page — the colour glow and the trend line rise into place — for a little more life.

On the Customers list, a customer's monthly cost and size band each get their own column now — and the size band uses the same tag style as Health and Status, so the three line up as one clean row instead of a small tag squeezed under the price. Sort by cost or by size.

A first-run welcome the first time you open the portal — set your display currency and timezone, then take a quick guided tour of how to onboard a customer. Re-open it any time from Get help → 'Take the tour'.
Its currency and timezone pickers use the portal's own on-theme dropdowns.
A first-run welcome the first time you open the portal — set your display currency and timezone, then take a quick guided tour of how to onboard a customer.
Re-open the tour any time from Get help → 'Take the tour'.
New Help center — open 'Get help' for pricing, a catalogue of every security finding and what it means, a getting-started guide, and an FAQ.
The Customers list now shows each customer's plan — size band and price — in its own column, and you can sort by it.
Prices across the portal now follow your currency picker, with the real NOK charge noted on billing.
The portal is now free to use — no license key and no license screens at all. The only thing you pay for is activating a customer tenant (a 'seat').
Onboarding a tenant and seeing its size and price stays free; that tenant's Identity, Conditional Access, Licenses and Backup data unlocks the moment you activate its seat.

Replace your license key on demand: a 'Replace key' button on the Billing page opens a dialog to paste a current Keygen key and activate it immediately — handy when a key was removed or replaced and the deployment is stuck on a stale one.
License re-check errors are clearer now — a plain-language reason (e.g. the key was rejected by Keygen) instead of a raw error dump.

The portal no longer locks you out when the backend is briefly unreachable (restarting or mid-deploy). It stays usable behind a small notice that clears itself once the backend responds again — and the rare 'license service unavailable' dialog is now centered and on-brand.
More room in the fleet Identity Health table: the Category column is wider, so long names like 'Multi-factor authentication' sit on a single line instead of wrapping onto two.

Billing now has a 'Re-check license' button — re-validate your license on demand instead of waiting for the daily sync. Handy if a renewal or change hasn't propagated yet, or to clear a stale 'license expiring soon' banner.

The summary cards on Identity, Conditional Access and Licenses now draw their own recent history as a small trend line under the number — open findings, criticals and total monthly license cost over time, matching the dashboard cards. The lines fill in as history accrues.

Fleet overview counts are live again: Active alerts and Open cases update the instant you resolve a case — no lag — and each headline now matches its own 'new / in progress' and 'assigned to you' subline.

Visual consistency: the colour-key dots on the overview, Licenses and Conditional Access cards are now squared to match the rest of the design, and a placeholder '?' tier badge was removed from the top bar.
Every fleet page (Identity, Conditional Access, Licenses, Backup) now has the same colour-coded summary cards as the dashboard — a subtle per-metric hue and glow instead of flat grey.
Billing is sortable: both the Subscription and Invoices tables sort by any column (tenant, cost, date, amount, status…), matching the rest of the portal.
A portal-wide typography pass — every page now uses one consistent text scale, so titles, body, labels and table headers line up in size and colour across the whole portal.

On a customer's Identity tab, the Findings and Categories cards now report the same number of categories (matching the tabs below), and clicking the Critical or High card jumps you straight to the relevant findings instead of force-opening one.
Finding drill-downs now match the rest of the portal: every column shows it can be sorted at a glance (not only on hover), and the 'How to fix' guides use the standard squared step markers and type.

A customer's Activity log no longer scrolls on forever: it now shows the 10 most recent events with a 'Show more' button to expand (and 'Show fewer' to collapse), plus a running 'Showing X of Y' count. Switching the bundle or action filter resets it to the latest 10.

New currency selector in the top bar: switch the whole portal between NOK (default), SEK, DKK, EUR, USD and GBP. License cost and waste figures convert instantly; your actual Stripe billing stays in NOK.
License Insights is clearer: the SKU inventory now shows clean product names with an Active / Stale / Unassigned colour key, sharper utilisation bars and larger, more legible figures.

The per-customer Cost trend is now a sparkline card matching the fleet overview — smooth line, subtle glow and a hover tooltip — and the Reclaim candidates' recommended action reads as a proper status tag.

Fleet overview redesigned: each KPI card now draws its own trend as a smooth, colour-coded sparkline; Open cases moved up under the cards for faster triage; and Alert volume is now an on-demand overlay where you can show, hide or isolate any incident category.

Customer Overview cards refreshed: colour-coded Active alerts, Identity findings, Conditional Access (policy count + guard mode) and Last backup — replacing the old Bundles and the duplicate Last-sync tile.

Polish throughout: incident owners always resolve to a name instead of a raw id, the customer search dropdown matches the portal (no typewriter font or off-palette blue), the Identity Health and Conditional Access tables breathe better, and scrollbars are themed to the dark UI.
Customers: the tenant ID now renders in JetBrains Mono, so the GUID's glyphs (0/O, 1/l/I) read unambiguously — easier to scan and copy — while the column spacing stays exactly where it was.

Inbox triage at fleet scale: a default 'By priority' view (most-critical first, so a Critical is never hidden) and an opt-in 'By customer' view that groups cases per tenant — worst-first, with a per-customer severity rollup and the customers that need action auto-expanded. Every column stays sortable, like the other tables.
Customers list: even breathing room across the left columns — the gap between Customer and Health now matches the Health-to-Status gap, and the table still fits narrower windows without clipping.

Customers list: more breathing room between the Customer, Health and Status columns (the 'Billing' column is now 'Status'), Health sits a little further to the right, and the Alerts column is a clean count instead of a dot.
Opening an incident now shows the same severity tag as the rest of the portal (the High orange), instead of an off-palette one.
Severity tags now read as a proper heat scale — Critical (red) and High (orange) are clearly distinct, then Medium (amber) and Low (grey).

Sorting is consistent across every list now: all columns are click-sortable through one shared header. Customers' Billing, the Inbox incident column, and the Backup and Licenses fleet tables are now sortable too (their default order is unchanged until you click a header).
Design polish: the “High” severity tag now matches the others (filled, not outlined), and every column on the Identity Health and Conditional Access lists clearly shows it can be sorted.

The portal-wide design refresh is complete: section headings, tables and the last status tags are now aligned across Settings, Licenses, Billing, Backup and the incident pages — every page follows one consistent system.
A cleaner, more consistent look across the portal: every status tag — health, billing, severity, backup and more — now shares one style, and the columns line up.

Calmer charts: the identity and conditional-access breakdowns and the alert-volume chart use a coordinated, muted palette instead of loud primary colours, so they read as data rather than alarms. Status colours (like red “Critical”) are kept where they carry meaning.

Customers you’ve just connected now show “Pending” on the Customers list until their first security scan completes — instead of an alarming “Warning”. It clears to a real Healthy, Warning or Critical status on its own, usually within minutes.
Hover a customer’s Health status to see what it means in plain language, plus that customer’s own open finding counts — critical, high, medium, low — and the risk score behind it.
Incident owners now show the analyst's name instead of an internal ID — across the inbox list, open cases and the incident page.
Manage subscription in Stripe now opens in a new tab, so you stay in the portal while updating billing and payment details.
In-app notifications now match the portal's design — the same card surface, the standard green check, and squared corners.
New Backup & Restore section: see your whole fleet's backup health at a glance — protected, stale, or no backup — and jump straight to any tenant's restore page.
Settings is tidier: Billing and Backup now have their own top-level sections instead of living inside Settings, which goes back to just configuration.
When a new customer grants consent, the welcome page now greets them by their organisation name and domain instead of a raw tenant ID.
Active tenants now have every feature fully working: the Identity, Conditional Access and Licenses tabs unlock AND load their data the moment a tenant is activated.
The 'No tenants active yet' banner clears once at least one tenant is active.
Active tenants now unlock every feature: the Identity, Conditional Access and Licenses tabs open as soon as a tenant is activated - no more locked tabs after you've paid.
The 'No tenants active yet' banner clears once at least one tenant is active.
New per-tenant billing: onboard tenants for free, then activate the ones you want from the Activate tenants page - each priced by its measured size. Replaces buying bundles and assigning seats.
One Basewiser product: Conditional Access Vault, Identity Health and License Insights are now a single product with every feature included.
Cleaner billing: the old per-tenant bundle-assignment page is gone - activation is the single, simpler flow.
Copying an invite now confirms it worked - Copy email, the consent link and the App ID show a 'Copied' tick when you click them.

The 'Set up the Basewiser app' step adds a plain-language 'What this does' explainer (the app and its credentials stay in your own Microsoft Entra tenant, each customer approves it once, you get read-only visibility plus Conditional Access remediation), and the setup button matches the rest of the portal.

Onboarding step 1 now checks off with a green tick and stays aligned with step 2 once the Basewiser app is set up - showing the app's name and ID without a heavy card. The setup button matches the portal's other buttons.
Once the Basewiser app is set up, the confirmation matches the version-update banner - a single blue mark with the app's name and ID - instead of a green 'Active' card.
The Add-tenant dialog buttons now match the rest of the portal - calm neutral buttons instead of a bold blue fill.

The email-invite instructions are clearer and harder to misread: labelled Option 1 (email the invite) and Option 2 (just send the link), step-by-step guidance that names each button and your mail app (e.g. Outlook), and a 'What this does' summary of what you send and what the customer's Global Administrator approves.

The email invite now says where it sends - Open in mail launches a new message in your default mail app (Outlook, etc.) - and adds a 'What this does' explainer covering what you send, what the customer's Global Admin approves, and what Basewiser can (and can't) see.
You can also just share the consent link instead of sending the full email - over Teams, chat, or an existing thread.

Sending an email invite now spells out the steps - copy the email, open a new message, paste it in - and adds an 'or just send the link' option for sharing the consent link over Teams, chat or an existing thread.
The invite email itself is redesigned: clearer layout with the Basewiser wordmark, a stronger call-to-action button, and labelled sections (it reads well in both light and dark mail clients).
Once the Basewiser app is set up, the panel states it's been created and ready to onboard tenants, and lists the app's name and App ID.
The first-run setup screen now matches the rest of the portal - same components, and once the Basewiser app is set up it shows the green Active panel with the app's name and App ID.

The Add-tenant dialog is polished and consistent with the rest of the portal: once the Basewiser app is set up it shows as an Active panel with the app's name and App ID (copyable), and the email-invite step is a single 'Open in mail' action that carries the branded message.
Invite emails render correctly in dark mode now (Outlook included) - the Basewiser wordmark adapts to the reader's theme instead of washing out.
First-run setup: opening a fresh portal now walks you through naming your organisation (the name customers see on invites) and setting up the Basewiser app - one screen, two steps.
After setup, the onboarding dialog shows your Basewiser app's name and App ID, with a spinner while it provisions.
Invite emails are branded now: Copy email gives you a formatted Basewiser message to paste into your mail client, and the invite reminds you which Partner identity it's sent as.
If app setup fails, the dialog names the exact Microsoft Graph permission the backend needs.
The onboarding dialog now notices if you delete the Basewiser app in Entra - it flips back to 'set up needed' instead of staying stuck on active, so you can re-create it cleanly.

Sending an email invite opens your own mail app with the subject and message (including the consent link) already filled in - just add recipients from your contacts and send. The in-portal recipient box is gone.
Polish: the two onboarding method cards line up, and the empty-state 'Add your first tenant' button is neutral grey like the rest of the portal.

Adding a tenant is now a guided two-step flow: set up the Basewiser app once (it's the single app every managed tenant consents to - one consent screen per customer instead of one per feature), then onboard tenants by branded email invite or directly. The onboarding panel is wider and spells out what each choice is for.
If app setup hits an error, the dialog now shows the actual reason inline instead of the button appearing to do nothing.
Partner identity (Settings) is simpler: set your display name and a support contact for tenant invite emails - the logo field is gone, invites use Basewiser branding.

Adding a tenant now starts with a choice, right from the Add tenant button: send a branded email invite the customer's own admin approves in one click, or add the tenant directly when you already hold an admin account in it.

New Onboarding page: connect a managed tenant two ways - onboard it directly when you hold an admin account in it, or generate a branded email invite that the customer's own admin approves in one click. Either way, the tenant registers itself in the portal once consent is granted.
Onboarding now runs on a single Basewiser app, so each customer approves one consent screen instead of one per feature.
Set the name customers see on the invite under Settings - Partner identity; it's pre-filled from your subscription and editable.
The tenant ID on Customers only copies from the copy icon now - the id itself is plain, selectable text, so a stray click no longer copies it.
Table columns are spread evenly across the width - the reclaim queue, fleet licensing and the licensing report no longer leave a big gap before the right-hand columns.
Status and empty-state icons now match the portal's squared corners - the 'all clear' check and the case-status glyphs (resolved, new) are squared instead of round.

Text across the portal is easier to read: descriptions, names, email and sign-in addresses, tenant IDs and other body text now sit at a consistent, comfortable size with a readable colour floor, instead of fine print. The break-glass section and the dense detail pages benefit most.
Layout lines up: the tenant detail and Zero Trust pages now use the same wide column as the rest of the portal, and the update / license banners match the page width instead of floating narrower.
On Customers, the tenant ID shows in full again - monospace, click to copy - instead of being cropped mid-string.
Selected filters are readable again - the active state is now a calm neutral highlight instead of blue text on a blue fill, across the Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access.

The Customers and Inbox lists read as a single table now, with the column header attached to its rows like Identity and Licenses. Inbox rows are calmer too: verdict tags (Auto-restored, Review sign-ins, GA) line up in their own column instead of crowding the title, the owner always shows a name rather than a raw id, and the description is trimmed so tenant, owner and age have room.

More squared-corner polish and faster triage: avatars and the resolved check-marks pick up the portal's squared corners, the Identity health summary cards are clickable (click Critical to filter to critical findings, worst first), the Licenses cards match the rest of the portal, and customer tenant IDs show a short head…tail you can click to copy the full id.

Every incident now tells its change story as a ledger on the affected policy: baseline, while the change was live, and now - with counts first (+ 5 excluded), names on demand, and the outcome stated outright (all removed - back at baseline). Readable in seconds even for big changes.
What-changed slims to the verdict and the raw diff - the story is told once, right next to the live state it explains. Timeline icons now match the portal's squared corners.

The incident page is redesigned: a calmer header with the owner shown by name (never a raw object-id), and Live policy state as a flat spec sheet - assignments collapse to clickable type counts and expand to a searchable list showing display names and sign-in addresses.
Small grey text across the portal is raised to a readable floor - sign-in addresses, owner names and customer tenant ids are no longer micro-print.
Audit attribution now records the operator's email even when the sign-in only carried a display name.
The 'update available' banner is calmer and gently animated, and the What's-new window is now a release timeline - every release since your version, newest first, with its change count.
Installing an update now shows real progress with an estimated time remaining instead of a plain spinner.

The Fleet overview is rebuilt: richer stat cards with honest trend badges, an alert-volume chart that stacks the four incident categories (Privilege escalation, Policy guard, Identity hygiene, Operations) from your real investigation log over the selected window, and an Open-cases table linking straight into each incident.
The whole portal now uses wide screens: the dashboard, Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access pages widen to the same cap the incident page got - more data, fewer dead margins.
Status gets a face: open cases carry the new status pill (dashed circle = new, spinner = in progress, green check = resolved) - the first piece of the refreshed component language.
Tab strips across the portal hug their content again instead of stretching edge to edge - the compact form reads better on wide screens.

What's new now accumulates: skip a release and its notes carry into the next banner. The portal shows everything since YOUR running version, grouped per release - no more updates silently replacing the notes you never read.

The incident page uses big screens properly: evidence and impact cards take the extra width while the playbook and timeline keep their comfortable size - no more content squeezed between dead margins.
Quiet polish: tab count badges stay the same calm grey whether or not the tab is active - selection reads from the tab itself. Severity-tinted finding counts keep their red and amber.

The Basewiser B is now the browser tab icon - the brand mark on a card tile matching the portal design, crisp from pinned tabs up to full-size bookmarks. If your tab still shows the old icon, a hard refresh clears the cached one.

The inbox is rebuilt for triage: every incident is its own card with sortable columns (severity, tenant, owner, age), an incident category on each row (Privilege escalation, Policy guard, Identity hygiene, Operations), and a quick-actions menu - assign to me, take over, open the customer, copy the link - without opening the case.

Filters speak one language everywhere: multi-select pills with built-in search and one-click clear on the Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access pages. Filter to two tenants and a category in three clicks; the X on the pill undoes it in one.

The Customers list gains search and sortable columns - sort by Alerts for the what's-on-fire view - and secondary tab rows across the portal are now full-width segmented strips, with the Identity tab reclaiming the space the old side table-of-contents held.

Role-grant alerts no longer reference an allowlist - there is no role allowlist; severity is purely tier-driven (GA above Tier 0, other roles lower). The change allowlist keeps governing guard-mode alerts, where it belongs.

Granter resolution is now three layers deep: the admin's own audit footprint resolves instantly, PIM schedule requests confirm intent (activation vs admin grant), and granter-less rows backfill for 24 hours - the WHO tile updates itself with a journal note.
Findings move with events: a role grant triggers the tenant's identity rescan immediately, and the active-alert badge updates the moment an incident is resolved.

Install this before the matching portal update, or with it. Basewiser no longer changes Conditional Access in a customer's tenant. Drift is still detected and backups are still taken — both are reads — and the fix itself is now yours to apply in your own admin session, from a Guided restore plan that lists the exact changes to make.

A new install asks for less. The consent screen no longer offers to change Conditional Access; every permission a customer's Global Administrator grants is a read. An existing install keeps working with no migration: a customer stored as Auto-Restore is read as Monitor on every scan and the stored setting is left untouched, which is what keeps the change reversible.

Drift that keeps coming back is now sold as a project. Three or more non-allowlisted drift events across two or more distinct policies in thirty days adds a change-control scope to that customer's Conditional Access opportunity — a named owner per policy, an approval path, a restore runbook — because a baseline that keeps moving is work somebody has to be paid to do.

Guard now checks a tenant once a minute by default, rather than every thirty seconds. Drift is found within a minute of happening instead of within thirty seconds; nothing else about detection changes, and the per-deployment schedule is still yours to set.
